tags.name: Issue Triggers
tags.description: Issue Triggers lets you setup rules that trigger issues when certain conditions are met.

tags.name: Attempts
tags.description: An attempt is any request that Hookdeck makes on behalf of an event.

tags.name: Bookmarks
tags.description: A bookmark lets you conveniently store and replay a specific request.

tags.name: Destinations
tags.description: A destination is any endpoint to which your webhooks can be routed.

tags.name: Bulk cancel events
tags.description: Bulk cancel operations allow you to cancel multiple pending events at once.

tags.name: Bulk retry events
tags.description: Bulk retry operations allow you to retry many events at once. A bulk retry is first estimated, then created, then processed asynchronously.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: An event is any request that Hookdeck receives from a source.

tags.name: Bulk retry ignored events
tags.description: Bulk retry ignored events allow you to retry many events that were previously ignored (for instance due to filter rules) at once.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description: An integration configures platform-specific behaviors, such as signature verification.

tags.name: Issues
tags.description: Issues lets you track problems in your project and communicate resolution steps with your team.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Query aggregated metrics for events, requests, and attempts with time-based grouping and filtering.

tags.name: Requests
tags.description: A request represent a webhook received by Hookdeck.

tags.name: Bulk replay requests
tags.description: Bulk replay requests re-runs the full pipeline for many historical requests through a chosen set of target connections. Useful for backfilling new connections and for reprocessing after a transformation change.

tags.name: Bulk retry requests
tags.description: Bulk retry requests allow you to re-ingest many previously received requests at once.

tags.name: Sources
tags.description: A source represents any third party that sends webhooks to Hookdeck.

tags.name: Transformations
tags.description: A transformation represents JavaScript code that will be executed on a connection's requests. Transformations are applied to connections using Rules.

tags.name: Connections
tags.description: A connection lets you route webhooks from a source to a destination, using a rule.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: An organization is the top-level entity that owns projects, members, and subscriptions.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: A project is an isolated environment that owns sources, destinations, and connections within an organization.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Notifications let your team receive alerts anytime an issue changes.

get.description: List the active organization and project API keys of the current organization. When called with an organization API key, secrets are only included for project keys whose scopes the calling key holds on that project; organization key secrets are never included. An organization API key limited to selected projects only lists the project keys of those projects.

post.description: Create an organization or project API key. Grants limit an organization key to specific projects; a project key is already limited to its own project. Creating organization API keys requires an admin session. Organization API keys can only create project keys, and only with scopes they hold on that project.

scopes.description: The scopes the key holds. Defaults to full access (`["*"]`) on create; omitted on update, the key keeps its current scopes. On an organization key limited to specific projects (see `grants`), these scopes apply in each of those projects. When the request is made with an API key, you can only give scopes that the calling key holds on the target project.

grants.description: The projects an organization key is limited to, keyed by project ID with `true` (or `{}`) as the value; the key uses its `scopes` in each of them. An organization key without grants works in every project; send `{}` on update to remove the limit. A project key is already limited to its own project, so grants don't apply to it.

post.description: Roll an API key: the current key expires after the rollover delay and a replacement key is returned. Organization API keys can only roll project keys whose scopes they hold on that project.

delay_sec.description: Seconds the current key stays valid after the roll

put.description: Update the scopes of an API key, and the projects an organization key is limited to (`grants`). The secret is unchanged. Organization API keys can only update project keys whose scopes they hold on that project, before and after the update.
